topic: A humanoid robot ran the 400m in 45.66 seconds
angle: The time is impressive; the running form is why everyone is watching
hook: A robot just ran the 400m in 45.66 seconds
caption:
Tiangong Omni took the 400m at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. The time is genuinely quick. The running gait is something else entirely — engineers optimised for stability and speed, not for looking human, and it shows in every stride.

slides.text: A robot just ran the 400m in *45.66* seconds
slides.subline: The form is the part nobody expected

slides.text: Everyone is sharing the time. The interesting part is that nobody designed it to look right — only to be fast.

slides.caption: the 400m, on two legs, with no human in the loop

slides.title: Why it looks wrong
slides.body: Human running form evolved for endurance and balance on uneven ground. A robot optimising purely for track speed converges on something that works and looks nothing like us.

slides.left_text: 43.03 seconds, held by Wayde van Niekerk since 2016.
slides.right_text: 45.66 seconds, on hardware you could buy a version of.

slides.title: What it signals
slides.body: Locomotion was the hard part of robotics for thirty years. It is now close to solved. The remaining problems are hands, judgement and cost.

slides.text: You won't see this anywhere else
